findings.title: Negative-offset slicing raises AssertionError on Django querysets
findings.body: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result intentionally slices the queryset with a negative start index when `enable_advanced_features` is set and `cursor.offset < 0` (line 880, `results = list(queryset[start_offset:stop])`). The comment claims "The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically," but this is false: Django raises `AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported` for any queryset sliced with a negative index. Since the audit log endpoint feeds an `AuditLogEntry.objects.filter(...)` QuerySet into this paginator, any request with a negative-offset cursor will crash with a 500 error instead of returning results. The same problem exists in the `is_prev` branch shared with BasePaginator (line 184), where `start_offset = offset` is used unclamped for previous-page cursors, so a client-crafted cursor like `0:-5:1` also produces a negative slice and a 500.

findings.title: `enable_advanced_features` is not an accepted argument of `Endpoint.paginate`
findings.body: The optimized branch calls `self.paginate(..., enable_advanced_features=True)`. Sentry's `Endpoint.paginate` (in sentry/api/base.py) has no `enable_advanced_features` parameter — extra paginator constructor arguments must be passed via the `paginator_kwargs` dict. Any request with `optimized_pagination=true` from a superuser or global-access member will raise `TypeError: paginate() got an unexpected keyword argument 'enable_advanced_features'` and return a 500, so the entire new code path can never succeed.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator is incompatible with datetime sort keys used by the audit log endpoint
findings.body: The endpoint instantiates OptimizedCursorPaginator with `order_by="-datetime"`, but the paginator's `get_item_key` (line 838-840) does `int(math.floor(value))` on the raw attribute, which is a `datetime` for this model. `math.floor` on a datetime raises `TypeError`, and unlike DateTimePaginator there is no strftime/multiplier conversion to a numeric epoch value. `get_item_key` is invoked by `build_cursor`/`_build_next_values` on every result, so even if the TypeError from the `paginate()` call signature were fixed, every optimized-path request would crash when building the next/prev cursors. The cursor values produced are also semantically different from DateTimePaginator's (raw value vs. milliseconds-since-epoch), so cursors are not interchangeable between the two paginators.

findings.title: Client-switchable paginator silently changes cursor semantics mid-pagination
findings.body: The paginator used depends on the per-request `optimized_pagination=true` query parameter. A client that pages through audit logs with the default DateTimePaginator receives cursors whose `value` is a milliseconds-since-epoch number (DateTimePaginator.multiplier = 1000); if the same client then sends that cursor with `optimized_pagination=true`, OptimizedCursorPaginator.value_from_cursor returns the raw integer and compares it directly against the `datetime` column in `build_queryset` (line 857). This produces wrong result windows (duplicated or skipped rows) rather than an error, because the two paginators disagree on the meaning of the cursor value. Cursor interpretation should not depend on an unrelated query flag toggled per request.

findings.title: No tests for the new paginator or the new endpoint branch
findings.body: The PR adds a new paginator class (OptimizedCursorPaginator), modifies the slicing logic in BasePaginator.get_result used by every cursor-paginated endpoint in the codebase, and adds a new request branch in the audit logs endpoint, but includes no tests. Basic coverage would have caught the crash-on-use defects (unsupported paginate kwarg, negative-offset slicing AssertionError, datetime key TypeError) and would guard the BasePaginator slicing change against regressions for existing consumers.

findings.title: Comment claims new negative-offset capability that the code does not implement
findings.body: The added comment states "Performance optimization: Allow negative offsets for advanced pagination scenarios / This enables efficient reverse pagination," but the code below it (`self.offset = int(offset)`) is unchanged from before — it already accepted any int. Meanwhile every other paginator in the codebase (OffsetPaginator, MergingOffsetPaginator, ChainPaginator, CombinedQuerysetPaginator) explicitly rejects negative offsets with `BadPaginationError("Pagination offset cannot be negative")`, and Django querysets cannot be sliced with negative indices at all. The comment documents a behavior that does not exist and contradicts the rest of the pagination stack, which will mislead future maintainers.
